newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tractebel CEO does not see Suez/Lyonnaise threat.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel CEO does not see Suez/Lyonnaise threat.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Belgian utility holding company Tractebel said on Thursday he did not see any direct threat from France's Lyonnaise des Eaux's plan to merge with Cie de Suez.

"Nothing will change officially for Tractebel. Our main shareholder will remain SGB and the Suez/Lyonnaise operation should not change our relations," Philippe Bodson told newspaper L'Echo in an interview published on Thursday.
The interview took place in New York.

French holding company Suez owns around 63 percent of SGB, which in turn owns 65 percent of Tractebel. SGB's Tractebel stake will fall to a little over 50 percent once Tractebel completes a planned full merger with its Belgian international energy utility operator Powerfin.

The Belgian government has sought assurances from SGB and Suez that Tractebel's freedom to operate in the energy sector will not be damaged by a Suez/Lyonnaise merger, which is expected to be finalised at two board meetings on Friday.
Tractebel controls Belgium's gas and electricity sectors through its Distrigas and Electrabel.

Bodson said Tractebel was willing to modify its statutes to explicitly prevent decisions of its board being unduly influenced by Lyonnaise, which also has international energy interests. Both groups are also active in waste management.
Bodson said he had been assured that Lyonnaise did not want Suez to sell any of its Belgian financial assets, "only some small operations in France."
Bodson said Tractebel and Lyonnaise could even cooperate in certain areas, without giving details.

"Our shareholders are conscious of the fact that we have won some contracts because we are Belgian. But that does not mean that collaboration, in certain cases, with Lyonnaise is to be excluded," Bodson said.
Bodson added he would not be interested in taking up a position on the board of Suez/Lyonnaise because that would represent "a conflict of interests."
